result.title: A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO
result.summary: Curriculum learning typically organizes training samples from easy to hard. In GRPO, medium-difficulty samples are attractive for online selection because they are more likely to yield informative group-relative learning signals, and prioritizing them can improve training efficiency. However, it remains unclear whether persistently selecting such samples also leads to the strongest final model performance, or whether training can benefit from progressing toward harder samples. Meanwhile, sample difficulty changes as the policy evolves, so fixed difficulty estimates can become misaligned with the current policy. We therefore re-estimate sample difficulty under the current policy and, inspired by the easy-to-hard principle of curriculum learning, design and evaluate a staged curriculum that progressively shifts the active difficulty band toward harder samples. Experiments on GSM8K show that persistent medium-difficulty selection does not achieve the strongest observed performance. Across three random seeds, progressing to a moderately harder difficulty band improves test accuracy to $0.6591 \pm 0.0077$, compared with $0.6449 \pm 0.0024$ for the fixed-medium curriculum. However, further progression to a harder difficulty band reduces accuracy to $0.6405 \pm 0.0053$. These results show that staged difficulty progression can outperform persistent medium-difficulty selection, but its benefit is non-monotonic. Effective GRPO curricula can therefore benefit from progressing beyond medium difficulty, while avoiding excessive progression toward overly difficult samples.}

AI.brief_summary: 该工作研究 GRPO 中课程难度递进对最终性能的影响：在当前策略下重新估计样本难度，并设计分阶段课程将活跃难度带逐步移向更难样本；GSM8K 上适度的难度推进优于持续选择中等难度，但进一步变难反而使准确率下降，收益呈非单调。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文为纯文本 RL 推理训练，未涉及视觉或 latent 状态，但其「随策略演化重估难度、按难度分阶段选择训练样本」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹训练的信号筛选与监督分配提供可核查线索。
